conventions.convention: Cell modules are right modules; right multiplication fixes the first cellular index. Higher ideals contain strictly larger cell labels. The left action is obtained through the cellular anti-involution.
The right tableau action is t·w=w⁻¹·t. Consequently d(t) is the inverse row-reading permutation, and Sμd uses distinguished representatives with length-additive products.
L₁=0 and Lₖ=Σⱼ<ₖ qʲ⁻ᵏT₍ⱼ,ₖ₎. Node content is column minus row; negative quantum integers satisfy [−m]q=−q⁻ᵐ[m]q.
Quantum characteristic is the least e≥2 with [e]q=0, or infinity. At q=1 it is the positive field characteristic, or infinity in characteristic zero.

Ordinary Specht modules are Sλ=(Sᴹλ′)θ, with θ(Tᵢ)=(q−1)−Tᵢ. Ordinary simple labels are e-regular; nonzero Murphy form quotients have e-restricted labels. Ordinary decomposition support is μ dominating λ.

S(d,n)=EndH(⊕μmμH), with ordinary endomorphism composition. Weight projections are identities on permutation summands. In the stable range d≥n, the Schur functor is X↦Xe and eSe≅H by left multiplication.

Beta sequences use conjugate parts: βᵢ=ν′ᵢ+L−i. Repeated or negative entries give zero symbols; otherwise sorting contributes its sign. Balanced shifts preserve degree, and Weyl symbols retain the row cutoff.
Jantzen layers are reduced filtration submodules (M(i)+πM)/πM, not successive quotients. The lift is finite free over a PID with chosen prime π and generically nondegenerate form.

Integral quantum calculations use A=Z[v,v⁻¹] and Hecke parameter q=v². Divided powers are integral matrices before specialization; the square-root-free generators are separately defined over Z[q,q⁻¹].

Polynomial highest modules carry specified nonnegative composition labels and full integral toral characters; specialized diagonal eigenvalues alone do not identify labels. Highest vectors are killed by every positive divided power.

load_bearing.statement: For every commutative ring R with invertible parameter z and composition ρ of n, xρHn has basis m(S,t)=Σs:ρ(s)=S mst, indexed by semistandard S and standard t of the same shape, and has an ordinary Specht filtration with the stated semistandard multiplicities. The Statement additionally asserts its displayed same-column generator refinement.

For every commutative ring R and unit q, the elements mst indexed by pairs of standard tableaux of equal partition shape form an R-basis and a dominance-cellular basis of H(R,q)(Sn), without a semisimplicity hypothesis.

S(d,n)=EndH(⊕μ∈Λ(d,n)mμH). Its normalized semistandard-pair maps form a dominance-cellular basis; its Weyl cells have semistandard bases, canonical form value one, nonzero absolutely simple heads over fields, and weight dimensions Kλμ.
For every commutative ring R and unit q, mₜLₖ=[contentₜ(k)]q mₜ+Σv strictly dominating t avmᵥ on each Murphy cell. The Lₖ commute pairwise, and every symmetric polynomial in them is central.

For a finite-dimensional unital cellular algebra over a field, the nonzero cell-form quotients are a complete set of pairwise non-isomorphic absolutely simple modules. A quotient is nonzero exactly when its form is not identically zero; only then is the form radical the unique maximal submodule and module radical.

Over every field F with unit q, Dλ is nonzero exactly for e(F,q)-regular λ; those quotients classify the absolutely irreducible Hecke modules. H is split semisimple if and only if e>n, including infinity; when e≤n its radical is nonzero.

Over a field with unit q and d≥n, F(Wλ)≅Cᴹ(λ) with exact restricted form factor one, and F(Lλ)≅Dᴹ(λ), including zero quotients. Surviving labels are e-restricted, and their composition multiplicities are preserved. The ordinary dictionary conjugates labels and applies θ to both modules.

For an integral domain, unit q, d,n≥1, and a Weyl weight space, its semistandard Gram determinant is qᴺ times the product of ([hab]q/[hac]q) raised to dμ(β+hac eb−hac ec), over pairs b<c in a row. The rational product is interpreted through its universal Laurent-polynomial identity, including singular specializations and empty weight spaces.

For the stated PID lift with [n]!q̂ nonzero, the sum of positive Weyl Jantzen-submodule classes equals the balanced signed hook-valuation sum. For d≥n the same identity transports to Murphy Specht filtration submodules. Multiplicity information uses the entire sum expanded in simple classes.

For A=Z[v,v⁻¹], q=v², N≥1 and r≥0, the integral divided-power tensor action preserves tensor space, commutes with its displayed Hecke action, and surjects onto the actual q-Schur endomorphism algebra. Its orbit-map preimages and specialized Hom basis survive arbitrary base change; a separately specified square-root-free generation assertion holds over every ring with unit q.

Every nonzero cell module of a finite-dimensional cellular algebra over a field lies in one block, including zero-form labels. Two nonzero cells share a block exactly when connected by a chain sharing simple composition factors. For one primitive idempotent per simple, dimF eμAeν=Σλ[Cλ:Dμ][Cλ:Dν]; empty cells contribute zero.

concerns.concern: The Statement displays Tₐmₛₜ ≡ −mₛₜ + Σu strictly less dominant than s cᵤmᵤₜ modulo higher shapes; F1 repeats that direction. This is false already in H(S₃). Let A=(1 2 / 3), B=(1 3 / 2), so A strictly dominates B, mAA=1+T₁ and mBA=T₂(1+T₁). Direct expansion gives T₁mBA+mBA+mAA=x(3), the higher row symmetrizer. Thus T₁mBA≡−mBA−mAA. B is the least dominant standard tableau of shape (2,1), so the displayed less-dominant sum is empty and cannot supply the nonzero correction mAA. The proof's prose instead says corrections are strictly more dominant. Reconcile the displayed Statement, F1 and proof direction, and check consumers using this refinement.
